note_en: A British word; in the US people say "trash can" or "garbage can".

def: a tall thing with places for books
example: There is a big bookcase in the living room.
example_ru: В гостиной стоит большой книжный шкаф.

def: a thing you put flowers in
example: There are red flowers in the vase on the table.
example_ru: В вазе на столе стоят красные цветы.
note_ru: Британцы говорят «ваз» (vɑːz), американцы — «вейс» (veɪs).
note_en: British speakers say /vɑːz/, Americans say /veɪs/.

def: a small thing you use to turn on the TV
example: Where is the remote control? I want to watch a film.
example_ru: Где пульт? Я хочу посмотреть фильм.

def: a room where you eat dinner
example: We eat dinner in the dining room.
note_ru: Это комната в доме; столовая как кафе — «canteen».
note_en: This is a room in a house; a dining area at work or school is a "canteen".

def: on or to a higher floor of a house
example: The bedrooms are upstairs.
note_ru: Без предлога: «go upstairs», а не «go to upstairs».
note_en: No preposition: "go upstairs", not "go to upstairs".

def: on or to a lower floor of a house
example: The kitchen is downstairs, next to the living room.

def: a soft thing you use to dry your body
example: There are clean towels in the bathroom.

def: a thing on the wall that shows the time
example: The clock on the wall says it's three o'clock.
example_ru: Часы на стене показывают три часа.
note_ru: «Clock» — часы на стене или столе; часы на руке — «watch».
note_en: A "clock" is on a wall or a table; one you wear on your wrist is a "watch".

def: a thing with four sides that you put things in
example: Put the old books in this big box.
example_ru: Положи старые книги в эту большую коробку.

def: a tall glass or plastic thing for water or milk
example: There is a bottle of water on the table.

def: a thing with points that you eat with
example: I need a knife and a fork, please.
example_ru: Мне нужны нож и вилка, пожалуйста.

def: a small round thing you eat soup with
example: Can I have a spoon for my soup?

def: a thing you use to make water hot
example: Put the kettle on. I want a cup of tea.
example_ru: Поставь чайник. Я хочу чашку чая.
note_ru: «Kettle» — чайник для кипятка; заварочный чайник — «teapot».
note_en: A "kettle" boils water; the pot for making tea is a "teapot".

def: a thing you listen to music and news on
example: My grandfather listens to the radio every morning.
example_ru: Мой дедушка каждое утро слушает радио.

def: a small machine that makes food hot fast
example: Put the soup in the microwave for two minutes.
example_ru: Поставь суп в микроволновку на две минуты.

def: a clock that wakes you up in the morning
example: My alarm clock rings at seven every day.
example_ru: Мой будильник звонит каждый день в семь.

def: a big picture you put on the wall
example: There is a football poster on the wall in my room.
example_ru: На стене в моей комнате висит футбольный плакат.

def: a soft red vegetable you eat in salad
example: I like tomatoes and cheese in my sandwich.
example_ru: Я люблю помидоры и сыр в сэндвиче.
note_ru: Британцы говорят «тэ-МА-тоу», американцы — «тэ-МЭЙ-тоу». Множественное число — tomatoes.
note_en: British speakers say /təˈmɑːtəʊ/, Americans say /təˈmeɪtoʊ/. The plural is tomatoes.

def: a round white vegetable with a strong taste
example: My mother cooks soup with onions and carrots.
example_ru: Моя мама варит суп с луком и морковью.

def: a long orange vegetable
example: Rabbits love carrots.

def: a long green vegetable with water in it
example: I eat cucumber and tomato salad in summer.
example_ru: Летом я ем салат из огурцов и помидоров.

def: a big round green vegetable with many leaves
example: My grandmother cooks soup with cabbage.
example_ru: Моя бабушка варит суп с капустой.

def: a small plant with a round top that you can eat
example: Do you want mushrooms on your pizza?

def: a yellow fruit that is not sweet
example: I drink tea with lemon.

def: a small round green or black fruit
example: We buy grapes and apples at the market.
example_ru: Мы покупаем виноград и яблоки на рынке.

def: a sweet green or yellow fruit
example: There are pears and apples in the garden.
example_ru: В саду растут груши и яблоки.

def: a small red fruit that is very sweet
example: Strawberries with cream are my favourite.

def: a small round red fruit on a tree
example: The children eat cherries in the garden.
note_ru: Одно слово и для вишни, и для черешни; кислая вишня — «sour cherry».
note_en: Russian has separate words for sweet and sour cherries; English uses cherry for both (a sour one is a "sour cherry").

def: a very big green fruit that is red inside
example: We eat watermelon on hot summer days.
example_ru: В жаркие летние дни мы едим арбуз.

def: cold food with vegetables
example: I have a salad with tomatoes for lunch.
example_ru: На обед я ем салат с помидорами.

def: Italian food made from flour, like spaghetti
example: We eat pasta with cheese on Fridays.
example_ru: По пятницам мы едим макароны с сыром.
note_ru: Неисчисляемое: «some pasta», а не «pastas».
note_en: Uncountable: "some pasta", not "pastas".

def: flat round bread with cheese and tomato on it
example: Let's have a pizza and watch a film.
example_ru: Давай съедим пиццу и посмотрим фильм.

def: long pieces of hot potato
example: I want fish and chips, please.
example_ru: Мне, пожалуйста, рыбу с картофелем фри.
note_ru: В Британии «chips» — картофель фри, а чипсы — «crisps». В США картофель фри — «fries».
note_en: In Britain "chips" are fried potato sticks and thin potato snacks are "crisps". In the US fried potato sticks are "fries".

def: very cold sweet food that children love
example: Do you want chocolate or strawberry ice cream?

def: sweet brown food that many people love
example: My sister likes chocolate cake.

def: a small, dry, sweet cake
example: We have tea and biscuits at four o'clock.
example_ru: В четыре часа мы пьём чай с печеньем.
note_ru: Британское слово; в США печенье — «cookie».
note_en: A British word; in the US: "cookie".

def: sweet food from fruit and sugar for bread
example: I eat bread with butter and jam for breakfast.
example_ru: На завтрак я ем хлеб с маслом и вареньем.

def: sweet yellow food that bees make
example: I like tea with honey when I am ill.
example_ru: Когда я болею, я люблю чай с мёдом.
note_ru: «Honey» — ещё и ласковое обращение: «дорогой / дорогая».
note_en: "Honey" is also a term of affection, like "darling".

def: long meat in a thin skin
example: We have eggs and sausages for breakfast.
example_ru: На завтрак у нас яйца и сосиски.

def: the food you eat at one time
example: Dinner is my favourite meal of the day.
example_ru: Ужин — мой любимый приём пищи за день.
note_ru: Завтрак, обед и ужин — это «meals»; сама еда — «food».
note_en: Breakfast, lunch and dinner are "meals"; the things you eat are "food".

def: a list of food in a restaurant
example: Can I see the menu, please?

def: good to eat
example: This soup is very tasty!

def: to hold something and take it with you
example: Can you help me carry these bags?
example_ru: Ты можешь помочь мне донести эти сумки?

def: to have something in your hand
example: Please hold my coffee for a minute.
note_ru: «Hold on!» по телефону — «Подождите, не вешайте трубку».
note_en: "Hold on!" on the phone means "Wait, don't hang up".

def: to take and hold something that is flying to you
example: The dog catches the ball every time.
note_ru: Также «catch a bus / train» — успеть на автобус / поезд.
note_en: Also "catch a bus / train": get on it in time.

def: to make pieces of something with a knife
example: Cut the bread with this knife, please.

def: to make something go into pieces
example: Be careful! Don't break the glass.

def: to put something in until it is full
example: Fill the bottle with water, please.

def: to move something to a place
example: Put the cups on the table, please.
note_ru: Одно слово и для «класть», и для «ставить».
note_en: Russian has separate verbs for laying something down and standing it upright; English uses put for both.

def: to go or take something to a new place
example: Can you move your bag? I want to sit here.
example_ru: Ты можешь убрать свою сумку? Я хочу здесь сесть.

def: to take something up with your hands
example: This box is very big. I can't lift it.
example_ru: Эта коробка очень большая. Я не могу её поднять.

def: to make a house or a wall
example: They are building a new school in our town.
example_ru: В нашем городе строят новую школу.

def: to get bigger, or to make plants bigger
example: We grow tomatoes in our garden.
example_ru: Мы выращиваем помидоры в нашем саду.
note_ru: «Grow up» — взрослеть, расти (о детях).
note_en: "Grow up" means to become an adult (about children).

def: to go up fast with your feet off the floor
example: The children jump and run in the park.
example_ru: Дети прыгают и бегают в парке.

def: to touch something very hard and fast
example: He hits the ball with his hand.

def: to put your hand on something
example: Please don't touch the pictures.

def: to look at something to see it is right
example: Check your email every morning.

def: to take the thing you want from many things
example: Choose a cake. They are all very good.
example_ru: Выбери торт. Они все очень вкусные.
note_ru: Не путайте «choose» (выбирать) и «chose» (выбрал).
note_en: Don't confuse "choose" (present) and "chose" (past).

def: to make something different or new
example: I want to change my phone. It is very old.
example_ru: Я хочу поменять телефон. Он очень старый.
note_ru: «Change money» — обменять деньги; «change trains» — сделать пересадку.
note_en: "Change money" = exchange it; "change trains" = move to another train on a journey.

def: to have something and not give it away
example: You can keep the book. I have a new one.
example_ru: Можешь оставить книгу себе. У меня есть новая.

def: to not have something and not know where it is
example: I always lose my keys!
note_ru: Не путайте «lose» (терять, luːz) и «loose» (свободный, luːs).
note_en: Don't confuse "lose" (/luːz/) and "loose" (not tight, /luːs/).

def: to be first or best in a game
example: Our team wins every football game.
example_ru: Наша команда выигрывает каждый футбольный матч.
note_ru: «Win a game» — выиграть игру, но «beat a team» — победить команду.
note_en: "Win a game", but "beat a team".

def: to say or do something again
example: Can you repeat the question, please?

def: to say the letters of a word
example: How do you spell your name?
example_ru: Как пишется ваше имя? (Назовите по буквам.)
note_ru: В британском английском — spelt, в американском — spelled.
note_en: British English: spelt; American English: spelled.

def: to go down to the floor fast
example: Be careful, don't fall! The floor is wet.
note_ru: «Fall asleep» — засыпать; «fall in love» — влюбляться.
note_en: "Fall asleep" = start sleeping; "fall in love" = start loving someone.

def: to start
example: The lesson begins at nine o'clock.
note_ru: «Begin» и «start» значат одно и то же; «begin» чуть более формальное.
note_en: "Begin" and "start" mean the same; "begin" is slightly more formal.

def: to push something with your finger
example: Press this button to open the door.
example_ru: Нажми эту кнопку, чтобы открыть дверь.

def: to move from standing to sitting
example: Please sit down and open your books.
forms: sit down – sat down – sat down
note_ru: «Sit down, please» звучит немного как команда; вежливее сказать «Have a seat» или «Take a seat».
note_en: "Sit down, please" can sound a bit like an order; "Have a seat" or "Take a seat" is more polite.

def: to move from sitting to standing
example: The students stand up when the teacher comes in.
forms: stand up – stood up – stood up

def: to put something on a table or the floor
example: Put your bag down here, please.
forms: put down – put down – put down
note_ru: Разделяемый глагол: «put it down», а не «put down it».
note_en: Separable verb: "put it down", not "put down it".

def: to go into a room or house
example: Come in and sit down.
forms: come in – came in – come in
note_ru: «Come in!» — так отвечают, когда кто-то стучит в дверь: «Войдите!».
note_en: "Come in!" is what you say when someone knocks on the door.

def: to return to a place
example: I go back to school on Monday.
example_ru: Я возвращаюсь в школу в понедельник.
forms: go back – went back – gone back

def: to turn your eyes to something
example: Look at this photo of my dog.
example_ru: Посмотри на это фото моей собаки.
note_ru: После «look» нужен предлог «at»: look at me, а не look me.
note_en: After "look" you need "at": look at me, not look me.

def: to stay until someone or something comes
example: We are waiting for the bus.
note_ru: По-русски «ждать кого-то» без предлога, а по-английски всегда «wait for somebody».
note_en: Russian uses no preposition here, but English always says "wait for somebody".

def: to go into a car or taxi
example: Get in the car, we are late!
forms: get in – got in – got in
note_ru: В машину или такси «get in», а в автобус, поезд или самолёт — «get on».
note_en: Into a car or taxi: "get in"; onto a bus, train or plane: "get on".

def: to leave a car, taxi or room
example: The taxi stops and we get out.
forms: get out – got out – got out

def: to wash the plates and cups after a meal
example: I cook and my brother washes up.
example_ru: Я готовлю, а мой брат моет посуду.
note_ru: В британском английском «wash up» — мыть посуду; в американском это «wash the dishes», а «wash up» значит умыться.
note_en: In British English "wash up" means to wash the dishes; in American English that is "wash the dishes", and "wash up" means to wash your hands and face.

def: to make a place clean and tidy
example: Let's clean up the kitchen after dinner.
example_ru: Давай уберём на кухне после ужина.

def: to do something faster
example: Hurry up! The film starts in five minutes.
example_ru: Поторопись! Фильм начинается через пять минут.
note_ru: Чаще всего используется в повелительной форме: «Hurry up!» — «Быстрее!».
note_en: Most often used as a command: "Hurry up!"

def: to write something on paper to remember it
example: Write down my phone number, please.
forms: write down – wrote down – written down
note_ru: Разделяемый глагол: «write it down», «write the number down».
note_en: Separable verb: "write it down", "write the number down".

def: to go down to the ground suddenly
example: The little boy fell down in the park.
forms: fall down – fell down – fallen down

def: to return something to its owner
example: Can you give me my pen back?
forms: give back – gave back – given back
note_ru: Разделяемый глагол: «give it back» или «give back the book».
note_en: Separable verb: "give it back" or "give back the book".

def: to take something to another place
example: Two coffees to take away, please.
forms: take away – took away – taken away
note_ru: В кафе «to take away» значит «с собой»; в американском английском говорят «to go».
note_en: In a café "to take away" means food you take with you; in American English people say "to go".

def: to phone someone again later
example: I'm busy now. Can I call you back?
example_ru: Я сейчас занят. Можно я тебе перезвоню?

def: to be born or live in a place
example: Where do you come from? – I come from Spain.
example_ru: Откуда ты родом? — Я из Испании.
forms: come from – came from – come from
note_ru: «Where do you come from?» и «Where are you from?» значат одно и то же.
note_en: "Where do you come from?" and "Where are you from?" mean the same.

def: to go or do something more slowly
example: Slow down, please. You speak very fast.
example_ru: Помедленнее, пожалуйста. Ты говоришь очень быстро.

def: to take something out of a bag or pocket
example: Take out your books and read page ten.
example_ru: Достаньте учебники и прочитайте страницу десять.
forms: take out – took out – taken out
note_ru: Также «take the dog out» — выгуливать собаку, «take the rubbish out» — выносить мусор.
note_en: Also "take the dog out" (for a walk), "take the rubbish out" (to the bin).

ru: есть не дома / ходить в ресторан
def: to have a meal in a restaurant
example: We eat out every Friday.
example_ru: Мы ходим в ресторан каждую пятницу.
forms: eat out – ate out – eaten out

def: to return with something from a place
example: My dad brings back presents from every trip.
example_ru: Папа привозит подарки из каждой поездки.
forms: bring back – brought back – brought back

def: to come home or to a place again
example: What time do you get back from work?
example_ru: Во сколько ты возвращаешься с работы?
forms: get back – got back – got back
note_ru: В разговорной речи «get back» встречается чаще, чем «return».
note_en: In everyday speech "get back" is more common than "return".

def: to not go to bed at night
example: Children, don't stay up late tonight.

def: to leave a place or a person
example: We are going away for the weekend.
forms: go away – went away – gone away
note_ru: «Go away!» в разговоре звучит грубо — «Уйди!», «Отстань!».
note_en: "Go away!" sounds rude in conversation.

def: you say this when something is not important
example: I'm sorry, I'm late. – Never mind.
note_ru: Также значит «забудь, не бери в голову», когда вы не хотите повторять сказанное.
note_en: Also means "forget it, it doesn't matter" when you don't want to repeat what you said.

def: a friendly way to say goodbye
example: See you tomorrow. Take care!
note_ru: Тёплое прощание между друзьями; часто так заканчивают письма и сообщения.
note_en: A warm goodbye between friends; often used to end letters and messages.

def: you say this when someone else can decide
example: Pizza or pasta? – It's up to you.

def: something that is very easy to do
example: The test was a piece of cake.
note_ru: Идиома; обычно с «a»: «It's a piece of cake».
note_en: An idiom; usually with "a": "It's a piece of cake".

def: you say this to agree or answer thanks
example: Thanks for your help! – No problem.
example_ru: Спасибо за помощь! — Не за что.
note_ru: Неформальный ответ на «thank you» или на просьбу.
note_en: An informal reply to "thank you" or to a request.

def: you say this to say yes strongly
example: Can I use your phone? – Of course.

def: you say this before someone does something hard
example: You have an exam today? Good luck!
note_ru: Часто с «with»: «Good luck with your exam!».
note_en: Often with "with": "Good luck with your exam!"

def: a friendly goodbye, often in shops
example: Here is your coffee. Have a nice day!
note_ru: Типичный ответ: «You too!» — «И вам!».
note_en: A typical reply: "You too!"

def: an informal hello or asking what is wrong
example: Hi, Tom! What's up?
note_ru: Очень неформально, только с друзьями. Можно просто ответить «Not much».
note_en: Very informal, only with friends. You can simply answer "Not much".

def: you say this to make someone hurry or try
example: Come on! We are late for the bus.

def: you say this when someone does something good
example: You got ten out of ten! Well done!
example_ru: У тебя десять из десяти! Молодец!
note_ru: В американском английском чаще говорят «Good job!».
note_en: In American English "Good job!" is more common.

def: you say this so someone takes food freely
example: There is fruit on the table. Help yourself.

def: you say this when you give something
example: Can I have the salt? – Here you are.
note_ru: Так же говорят «Here you go» или «There you go».
note_en: People also say "Here you go" or "There you go".

def: you say this when you are sad about something
example: I can't come to your party. – What a pity!
example_ru: Я не смогу прийти на твою вечеринку. — Как жаль!

def: you say this when you feel the same
example: I love chocolate. – Me too!
note_ru: После отрицания говорят «Me neither»: «I don't like fish. – Me neither».
note_en: After a negative sentence say "Me neither": "I don't like fish. – Me neither".

ru: Мне всё равно. / Я не против.
def: you say this when both choices are fine
example: Tea or coffee? – I don't mind.
example_ru: Чай или кофе? — Мне всё равно.
note_ru: Вежливый ответ; «I don't care» звучит грубее — «мне плевать».
note_en: A polite answer; "I don't care" sounds ruder, like you have no interest at all.

def: you say this when very surprised or saying no
example: I won a car! – No way!

def: you say this when there is danger
example: Watch out! There is a car!
note_ru: Так же говорят «Look out!» и «Be careful!».
note_en: People also say "Look out!" and "Be careful!"

def: you say this when someone sneezes
example: Atchoo! – Bless you!

def: you say this to ask for a short wait
example: Just a moment, please. I'm coming.
note_ru: Также «Just a minute» и «Just a second» — все три значат одно и то же.
note_en: Also "Just a minute" and "Just a second": all three mean the same.

def: you say this to make someone calm
example: Don't worry, the doctor is here.

def: you say this when there is no hurry
example: Take your time, the shop is open till nine.
example_ru: Не спеши, магазин открыт до девяти.

def: a person who watches TV all day
example: My brother is a couch potato at the weekend.
example_ru: Мой брат по выходным — настоящий лежебока.
note_ru: Шутливая идиома, не обидная среди друзей.
note_en: A jokey idiom, not offensive among friends.

def: a person who gets up very early
example: My mum is an early bird. She gets up at six.
example_ru: Моя мама — ранняя пташка. Она встаёт в шесть.
note_ru: Противоположность — «night owl» (сова).
note_en: The opposite is "night owl".

ru: Сколько лет, сколько зим! / Давно не виделись!
def: you say this to a friend after a long time
example: Hi, Anna! Long time no see!
note_ru: Неформальное приветствие; грамматически странное, но все так говорят.
note_en: An informal greeting; grammatically odd, but everyone says it.
